rows.t: Cleveland Browns 1998 "No Fan Like a Browns Fan" Poster w/ Cert of Authenticity

det.desc: "No Fans like a Browns Fan" Poster This is a unique item that I have not been able to find on eBay or other services. It is a good BUY. comes with its Certificate of Authenticity Commissioned By: Cleveland Browns 1997 Produced By: Marcus Advertising Art Director: Brian Roach Publishing By: AMERIPRO Publishing Printing Date: March 20, 1998 Edition Number: 001 Number of Prints: 25,000 Printing Process: 4-color Image Size: 24" x 36" Paper Stock: 100 lb. Gloss Book Signed By: Michael Haemmer (publisher) There are no additional proofs except as above stated. The Transfer medium and plate have been cancelled. rows.t: Mid-century Brass Rooster

det.desc: Decorative brass animal figurines gained immense popularity during the mid-20th century, particularly within Hollywood Regency and transitional interior design schemes. Artisans often utilized lost-wax or sand-casting techniques to achieve highly textured surfaces that caught the light and added dramatic flair to home decor. Roosters, symbolizing vigilance and courage, were frequently cast as paired fighting or strutting display pieces for dining rooms and entryways. Many of these expressive brass sculptures were produced in European foundries, notably in Italy and parts of Spain, before being exported to American department stores and interior design boutiques. The rich patinas and meticulous feather detailing reflect a period when heavy, sculptural brass accessories were a hallmark of sophisticated interior styling. The iconic trumpet or Jack-in-the-Pulpit silhouette became exceptionally popular during the mid-20th century as modern interior design embraced dramatic, organic forms and vibrant color palettes. Techniques such as rigati or optic ribbing and contrasting rim applications showcase the high level of skill required by Venetian gaffers working at the furnace. Mid-century Italian glass factories exported these decorative pieces worldwide, making them prized centerpieces in homes adopting eclectic or atomic-era aesthetics.
